study.title: Natural products against renal fibrosis: molecular mechanisms, safety concerns, and translational perspectives

cover.headline: Plant compounds target **seven distinct mechanisms that drive kidney scarring**, but translation lags the lab.

slides.title: Chronic kidney disease progresses to end-stage failure through a scarring process called renal fibrosis.
slides.body:
Current therapies can slow the decline, but they cannot reverse fibrosis once the scarring has set in. That gap leaves millions of patients on a one-way path toward dialysis or transplant.

Researchers have turned to natural products—flavonoids, alkaloids, terpenoids, and other plant-derived compounds—because they act on multiple biological pathways at once. The question is whether these compounds can target the mechanisms that sustain kidney scarring.

slides.title: Natural products interfere with inflammation, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, autophagy, epigenetics, and cell death.
slides.body:
This review compiled evidence showing that defined bioactive compounds—not crude extracts—modulate at least seven overlapping pathological processes linked to fibrosis. Each pathway contributes to the remodeling that stiffens kidney tissue and erodes function.

Advances in separation and purification now allow researchers to isolate single active molecules and test them in controlled lab settings, moving beyond the unpredictable mixtures used in traditional preparations.

caveats: This is a review summarizing lab and mechanistic studies, not a clinical trial testing natural products in patients.
The abstract does not specify which compounds were tested, in what species, or at what doses.

caption: Plant-derived molecules may disrupt the biological cascades that turn chronic kidney disease into irreversible scarring. The review, published in Renal Failure, maps how flavonoids, alkaloids, terpenoids, glycosides, polyphenols, quinones, and related compounds interact with inflammation, oxidative stress, mitochondrial function, metabolism, autophagy, epigenetic marks, and programmed cell death—all processes implicated in renal fibrosis. The authors note that purification technology has shifted focus from crude extracts to isolated bioactive agents. This is a mechanistic review, not a human trial. Full study: doi.org/10.1080/0886022x.2026.2703925 — What needs reversing most?

unsupported_claims.claim: Plant compounds target **seven distinct mechanisms that drive kidney scarring**
unsupported_claims.problem: The abstract does not specify the number seven. It lists 'inflammation, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, metabolic reprogramming, autophagy dysregulation, epigenetic regulation, and regulated cell death' - which is indeed seven mechanisms - but the abstract never states 'seven' or quantifies them as such.
The abstract does not state the number seven. This is a count derived from listing the pathways mentioned, but the number itself does not appear in the abstract.
